req.title: Return 404 for unknown routes
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 for any path not matching a defined route.

doc.reasoning: R-HTTPBIN-036 requires that any path not matching a defined route returns HTTP 404. Tests must cover: (1) a clearly unknown path returns 404 (EP positive of the error pathway), (2) a known valid route returns 200 (EP positive of the success pathway, proving the 404 logic is selective), (3) boundary paths that are near-misses of real routes (BVA), (4) various HTTP methods on unknown routes (DT), and (5) deeply nested unknown paths (NEG). Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting the exact status code 404 (not >= 400, not 403, not 405), asserting 200 for known routes (catches mutations that make everything 404), and testing multiple unknown paths to prevent constant-substitution mutations from surviving.

tests.name: test_unknown_route_returns_404_get
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Path /this-route-does-not-exist is not registered in httpbin
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send GET request to /this-route-does-not-exist
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 404
trace: R-HTTPBIN-036: system shall respond with HTTP 404 for any path not matching a defined route
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_unknown_route_returns_404_get():
    r = client.get('/this-route-does-not-exist')
    assert r.status_code == 404
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 302
    assert r.status_code != 400
    assert r.status_code != 403
    assert r.status_code != 405

test_unknown_route_returns_404_get()

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_near_miss_route_get_suffix_returns_404():

    assert r1.status_code == 404
    assert r1.status_code != 200
    r2 = client.get('/ge')

import json
client = app.test_client()

def test_known_headers_route_returns_200_not_404():
